exposure: timing of hypothyroidism diagnosis (pre-pregnancy vs during pregnancy)
cohort: 452 pregnant women with hypothyroidism at a tertiary care center in Bengaluru, India over a 2 year period
finding: There was no difference in pregnancy outcomes (congenital hypothyroidism, birth weight, abortion rate) between women diagnosed with hypothyroidism before pregnancy and those diagnosed during pregnancy, although women diagnosed pre-pregnancy presented earlier for testing.
mod_finding: There was no difference in number of cesarean sections, abortions and low birth weight babies between overt and subclinical hypothyroidism subgroups.
birth_weight: Mean birth weight was 2.90 ± 0.39 kg in Group I (pre-pregnancy hypothyroidism) versus 2.88 ± 0.36 kg in Group II (hypothyroid during pregnancy); P = 0.608
